conviction_note: The findings offset to an impact_sum of 0.0. Proxy negatives: the full-year consensus of $0.83-0.85 sits at the top of a $0.75-0.85 guide that, after H1's actual $0.50 and Q3's $0.15 consensus, needs a flat-YoY Q4; record diesel; Bimbo share gains. They are matched by a crowded short of about 22% of shares, a Q3 bar already set 35% below last year, and category scanner units improving from August to September. p_up is 48 because the guide-risk lean is almost cancelled by the squeeze mechanism and by this name's muted reaction to bad news (Q2 miss plus guide cut: -2.1%) against its large reaction to relief (Q1: +13.3%). abs_move is 9%, not the sealed 17.2%: that straddle sits on a 7.5 strike against a 6.40 spot with a 67% spread, so I scaled from 62% realised volatility and the last three reactions (13.3, 8.7, 2.1) instead.
bar: Q3 FY2026 (12 weeks to ~2026-10-10). Adjusted EPS bar is $0.15, from two agreeing sources: Chartmill (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/FLO/estimates) and Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-04 (https://finviz.com/news/416236/flowers-foods-faces-a-volume-test-as-guidance-leans-on-unproven-fourth-quarter-recovery; whisper $0.16). Benzinga carries $0.16. Revenue bar is about $1.19B on all three, against $1.231B and $0.23 a year ago. Company FY2026 guide from the 2026-08-20 release (https://investors.flowersfoods.com/~/media/Files/F/Flowers-Foods-V3/documents/events/q2-2026/flowers-foods-inc-reports-second-quarter-2026-results.pdf): net sales $5.070-5.142B, adjusted EBITDA $453-481M, adjusted EPS $0.75-0.85. FY EPS consensus is disputed: Earnings Whispers says $0.85 with revenue of $5.17B, above the guided ceiling; a second aggregator says $0.83. So the FY bar is unsourced to two agreeing sources, and the guidance finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 46.4M shares and 6.7 days to cover (ShortSqueeze.com, page dated 2026-10-29, https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=FLO). Fintel gives 46.49M shares, 23.72% of float and 7.46 days to cover (https://fintel.io/s/us/flo, price date 2026-10-02). A secondary piece cites about 17% of float and 7.8 days on a 2026-10-20 report (https://macmyths.com/defensive-plays-are-gaining-steam-5-heavily-shorted-names-that-could-pop/). Against 212.06M shares outstanding (10-Q cover, 2026-08-14) that is about 22% of shares. This is a crowded short. Skew is null in the baseline. The front-expiry put/call OI ratio is 0.48 on only 1,705 contracts, and the ATM spread is 67% of mid, so the option market makes no usable directional statement. Sell-side sentiment is washed out: Jefferies Hold with the target cut from $7 to $6 (2026-10-06), Exane BNP Sell at $5 (2026-10-07), and a MarketBeat consensus of 'Reduce' with an average target of $6.80, against a $6.395 spot. The stock is -46.5% from its 52-week high, -9.9% over 5 days and +4.5% over 20 days, having bounced from $5.89 on 2026-10-08.

findings.finding: The full-year consensus ($0.85 per Earnings Whispers, $0.83 elsewhere) sits at or near the top of the $0.75-0.85 adjusted EPS guide. H1 actual is $0.50 (Q1 $0.29 + Q2 $0.21) and Q3 consensus is $0.15, so consensus needs Q4 at $0.18-0.20. Last year's Q4 was $0.22 including $0.02 from the 53rd week, about $0.20 on a 12-week basis, so that is roughly flat year on year. Every 2026 quarter has been down 15-35%. Holding the guide midpoint ($0.80) implies Q4 of about $0.15 (-25% YoY), and a narrowing toward the low end would take the FY consensus down about 5-12%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-02-12, a first FY2026 guide below expectations: -8.72%. 2026-08-20, Q2 miss plus FY guide cut: only -2.11%. 2025-08-15, guide cut: -5.37%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market believed the low end, the aggregator FY consensus would sit at or below $0.80, not $0.83-0.85. The Q3-plus-Q4 arithmetic has not been carried through to the FY number in the aggregators. Against that, the sell-side targets ($5-6) and the stock at about 8x the guide midpoint suggest the price already discounts more than the aggregator consensus does, which is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: The H1 actuals come from the company's own Q2 release (https://investors.flowersfoods.com/~/media/Files/F/Flowers-Foods-V3/documents/events/q2-2026/flowers-foods-inc-reports-second-quarter-2026-results.pdf). The Q4 2025 base of $0.22 including the $0.02 extra week comes from the Q4 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1128928/000119312526048756/flo-ex99_1.htm). The consensus figure has one primary source; the second aggregator disagrees by $0.02.

findings.finding: Input costs rose inside the reported quarter (2026-07-19 to ~10-10). US diesel hit a record $6.29/gal in September 2026, +68% YoY (EIA, via the Star-Advertiser, 2026-09-18), and Axios on 2026-08-30 had wheat and corn at three-year highs. The August guide assumed 'market and competitive conditions remaining generally consistent' and already named higher freight costs as a Q2 margin drag and fuel and commodity costs as 'increasing' headwinds into 2027. Both hurt Q3 SD&A/freight and argue for a cautious Q4 and 2027 tone.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior: cost-driven margin misses were bundled with volume misses in the 2025-08-15 (-5.37%) and 2026-08-20 (-2.11%) prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Management flagged 2027 fuel and commodity headwinds on 2026-08-20, so the direction is known. What the guide could not hold is the September diesel record that came after it. If that were priced, FY consensus would have moved to the low end of the guide, and it has not (see the guidance finding). Partly priced: the staples group trades on oil (FLO +4.4% on 2026-11-02 when oil fell on US-Iran talk hopes, https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/flo/news/why-up-down/flowers-foods-and-inter-parfums-shares-are-soaring-what-you-need-to-know).
findings.independence: This is a macro-to-company proxy that the company has not confirmed for Q3. The company's own 2026-08-20 prepared remarks name fuel and commodity costs as rising 2027 headwinds (https://investors.flowersfoods.com/~/media/Files/F/Flowers-Foods-V3/documents/events/q2-2026/q2-2026-results-prepared-remarks-transcript.pdf). The 10-Q tags wheat, corn, soybean oil and natural gas hedges; no fuel hedge is visible.

findings.finding: Circana category units improved through Flowers' Q3. Total US bakery units were -4.3% YoY in August and -2.4% in September (dollars -2.5% then -0.9%). Aisle (center-store) bakery units were -3.1% in September, with aisle bread units -3.5% and aisle buns and rolls units +2.5%. Flowers' own Q2 volume was -5.8% (branded -7.6%), and it said Q4 volumes should stabilise. The revenue bar ($1.19B, -3.3% YoY against Q2's -4.0%) already assumes a small improvement, and the category data supports reaching it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume is the line FLO trades on. Q2 volume -5.8% with a revenue miss took the stock -2.11% together with the guide cut. The Q1 beat (branded growth +3.4% with Simple Mills) took it +13.27%.
findings.why_not_priced: Trade-press category data is not carried in the earnings previews, which frame Q4 stabilisation as 'unproven'. If it were priced, the preview narrative would cite sequential improvement. It is a category proxy, not Flowers' own share, so it is small.
findings.independence: Perishable News / ABA review of the same Circana month, 2026-10-26 (https://perishablenews.com/?p=437073), so it shares a data source. August aisle bakery units were -5.4% (https://theshelbyreport.com/2026/09/23/perimeter-bakery-holds-up-better-than-center-store-in-tough-august/).

findings.finding: Grupo Bimbo, Flowers' largest fresh-bread competitor, reported Q3 2026 (2026-10-22/23) after Flowers last spoke. North America sales were +1% ex-FX on favourable price/mix with lower volumes, adjusted EBITDA margin was +40bp to 10.8%, and it gained share in four of six North American categories. Share Bimbo gains in sandwich bread and buns is likely partly Flowers' loss. Bimbo's positive pricing also argues against an intensifying price war.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 commentary blamed 'sustained competitive activity' and competitors not following Flowers' price increases; that print took the stock -2.11%.
findings.why_not_priced: A Mexican-listed peer's print is not in FLO's US previews; neither the Nov-4 Earnings Whispers preview nor the aggregators mention it. It is two-sided (share loss against rational pricing), so it is small.
findings.independence: Bimbo Q3 summary on Quartr (https://quartr.com/events/grupo-bimbo-bimbo-q3-2026_ojNHOKiB) and Baking Business coverage (https://www.bakingbusiness.com/articles/67133-bimbos-growth-streak-extended-in-third-quarter); all rest on Bimbo's one release.

findings.finding: Crowded short into a washed-out name. About 46.4M shares are short (about 22% of the 212M shares outstanding; Fintel puts it at 23.7% of float), with 6.7-7.5 days to cover. Sell-side targets of $5-6 sit at or below the $6.40 spot, and the stock fell 9.9% in the five sessions before the print. The last relief print (Q1, 2026-05-21: a beat plus the dividend reset) went +13.27%. An in-line Q3 with the guide held and any volume stabilisation evidence gives covering a mechanism of its own.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-05-21: +13.27% on a $0.29 vs $0.26 beat with a dividend halving. 2026-08-20: bad news (miss plus guide cut) took only -2.11%, a damped downside.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public, but the squeeze is conditional on the print. If shorts were already covering, the stock would not have fallen 9.9% in the five days before the print, and the borrow would be shrinking rather than holding at about 46M shares across the October settlements.
findings.independence: Fintel, 2026-10-02 (https://fintel.io/s/us/flo): 46.49M shares, 23.72% of float, 7.46 days. A secondary piece cites 17% and 7.8 days from a 2026-10-20 report (https://macmyths.com/defensive-plays-are-gaining-steam-5-heavily-shorted-names-that-could-pop/). The bearish analyst targets are a separate source: Jefferies $6 on 2026-10-06, Exane $5 on 2026-10-07 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FLO/analyst-ratings).

findings.finding: The Q3 EPS bar of $0.15 is a 35% YoY decline on a 3.3% revenue decline, deeper than Q2's -30% (0.30 to 0.21) on -4.0% revenue. Q2's release also cited moderating ingredient costs, about $9M of reorganisation savings in the rest of 2026, and new business wins ramping in Q3/Q4. Repeating Q2's rate of decline gives about $0.16, which is the whisper. The opposing cost proxy is netted in the input-cost finding.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats: Q1 2026 +$0.03 gave +13.27% (with the dividend news). 2025-11-06 Q3 2025 gave +1.89%. EPS miss: Q2 2026 -$0.01 gave -2.11%.
findings.why_not_priced: The whisper ($0.16) is already a penny above the bar, so a one-cent beat is partly expected. What is not in it is a beat larger than the whisper. This is inference from the company's own run rate, so it is small.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers bar and whisper, 2026-11-04 (https://finviz.com/news/416236/flowers-foods-faces-a-volume-test-as-guidance-leans-on-unproven-fourth-quarter-recovery); Chartmill bar $0.15 (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/FLO/estimates).

findings.finding: The Chief Human Resources Officer (Cindy Cox) sold 4,400 shares in the open market at $5.89 on 2026-10-08, keeping 41,030. It is the only Form 4 since the Q2 print, and no insider bought at the lows.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a month; trivial size.

findings.finding: An 8-K of 2026-11-04 (items 5.02 and 9.01) elected two former packaged-food CFOs to the board, effective 2026-11-18, both on the audit and finance committees: Shaun Mara (Simply Good Foods) and Ken Plunk (J&J Snack Foods). Read as a strengthening of capital-allocation and balance-sheet oversight ahead of the Q3 print; it gives no direction for the window.
findings.why_not_priced: Public; the stock rose on the day with the staples group, not on this.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-02 Flowers recalled 20oz and 40oz Nature's Own Hawaiian Bread for undeclared milk. Distribution was in AR, LA, NM, OK and TX, with no illnesses reported. That is a small regional cost inside Q4, on the brand being relaunched.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and immaterial; filed for completeness.

findings.finding: Financing. The $400M of 3.5% notes due October 2026 were pre-funded by a $400M delayed-draw facility, which management said 'completely de-risks' the maturity (2026-08-20 remarks). An automatic shelf (S-3ASR) followed on 2026-08-28. Asked what the money buys: the facility refinances a maturity, not a ramp, and nothing visible indicates an equity raise. The shelf reads as a routine WKSI renewal, so this is signed zero.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none; the May 2026 dividend halving to cut leverage below 3x took the stock +13.27% with the Q1 beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Public. The only window-relevant piece is the Q3 leverage print against the sub-3x target, which the call will update.
findings.independence: Q2 prepared remarks on the delayed-draw facility (https://investors.flowersfoods.com/~/media/Files/F/Flowers-Foods-V3/documents/events/q2-2026/q2-2026-results-prepared-remarks-transcript.pdf).

outside_window.finding: The formal FY2027 outlook normally comes with the Q4 release in February. Management has already flagged rising 2027 commodity and fuel headwinds, so any Q3-call colour is a preview, but the numeric 2027 guide resolves after the window.

baseline_tension: The baseline carries no skew and an unreliable straddle. The -9.9% five-day run-in and the 22%-of-shares short cut against my small negative guidance and cost proxies, and they leave the set balanced at zero.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short, about 22% of shares, 6.7-7.5 days): shrank the negatives. Input-cost proxy -1.2 to -0.9; Bimbo share finding -0.5 to -0.4.
Lesson 6 (the FY bar is disputed, $0.83 against $0.85, with one primary aggregator): capped the guidance finding, -1.5 to -1.0.
Lesson 5 (macro-to-company proxy): kept the diesel/wheat finding filed and small, with independence marked as a proxy.

Lessons 1 and 8 and the core's understatement note: abs_move raised from 8 to 9 (62% realised volatility, recent reactions of 13.3 and 8.7), and p_up moved from 47 to 48 because bad news has been damped on this name.
Lesson 4: financing finding left at 0 after asking what the money buys (refinancing a maturity).
